full_text_en:
Li Jinlian and Li Naping v. Ke Jiesheng — dispute over house pawn redemption

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Ke Jiesheng, male, 40 years old, from Zhangzhou City, Fujian Province.

Agent ad litem: Chen Xiuzhen (spouse of Ke Jiesheng).

Agent ad litem: Zeng Huaqun, lawyer of Xiamen No. 2 Law Firm, Fujian Province.

Appellees (Plaintiffs at First Instance): Li Jinlian, female, 61 years old, from Taipei City, Taiwan Province, residing at No. 174 Fuxing Road, Taipei City.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Li Naping, female, 44 years old, from Xiamen City, Fujian Province, residing at No. 30 Kunming Street, Taipei City.

Agent ad litem: Li Qiguang, cadre of Kaiyuan District Juvenile Sports School, Xiamen City, Fujian Province.

Appellant Ke Jiesheng, dissatisfied with the civil judgment of first instance rendered by Kaiyuan District People's Court of Xiamen, Fujian Province, in the dispute over house pawn redemption, appealed to Xiamen Intermediate People's Court.

Ke Jiesheng's grounds of appeal are: 1. Although the original pawnor and pawnee resided respectively in Taiwan Province and the Philippines before liberation, the two places could communicate with each other. The pawnor party proposed redemption 36 years after the expiration of the pawn period for the house in dispute, which has exceeded the redemption period. According to relevant provisions, it should be regarded as a forfeited sale. 2. The appellant is only one of the heirs of the pawnee and has no authority to represent other legitimate heirs in the litigation. He requests to add other heirs of the pawnee Ke Boxing to participate in the litigation.

Upon public trial, Xiamen Intermediate People's Court found: The bungalow located at No. 10 Beimenwai Street, Xiamen City, was the property of Li Qijing, husband of appellee Li Jinlian and father of appellee Li Naping. In November 1948, Li Qijing pawned two rooms, one hall, and an empty lot behind the hall within the courtyard, totaling 140 square meters, to Ke Boxing, grandfather of appellant Ke Jiesheng. The pawn period was five years (from November 1948 to October 1953), with a pawn consideration of USD 250. During the pawn period, Li Qijing went to Taiwan to seek a livelihood and died in 1975. Ke Boxing went to the Philippines and died in 1960. In October 1989, Li Jinlian and Li Naping filed a lawsuit with Kaiyuan District People's Court on the ground that Li Qijing had gone to Taiwan to seek a livelihood early on, and due to the long-term separation across the Taiwan Strait, the house pawned to Ke Boxing was difficult to redeem upon expiration of the pawn period. The court rendered judgment: Li Jinlian and Li Naping are permitted to redeem the house pawned by Li Qijing to Ke Boxing; Li Jinlian and Li Naping shall pay RMB 5,000 to the legitimate heirs of Ke Boxing, defendant Ke Jiesheng, within seven days after the judgment takes legal effect.

Xiamen Intermediate People's Court, upon trial, held: The pawned house that appellees Li Jinlian and Li Naping seek to redeem, according to the judicial interpretation of the Supreme People's Court regarding cases where the pawn period has expired over ten years or where the pawn period is not specified and exceeds thirty years without redemption, has exceeded the redemption period and should in principle be regarded as a forfeited sale. However, the judicial interpretation of the Supreme People's Court also provides that where the pawn period has expired and the pawnor is unable to redeem due to force majeure, the time exceeding the contractually specified period shall be deducted and not counted in the limitation period for redemption. For the house in dispute in this case, prior to November 1987 when the Taiwan authorities allowed Taiwanese compatriots to return to the mainland for family visits, due to historical reasons, the long-term separation across the Taiwan Strait prevented the pawnor from claiming redemption. This situation should be regarded as force majeure, and this period should not be counted in the redemption period. According to the above provisions, the pawnor's claim for redemption of the pawned house has not exceeded the time limit. At the same time, the pawnor's inability to exercise its claim within the statutory limitation period due to the same reason constitutes a "special circumstance" under Article 137 of the General Principles of Civil Law of the People's Republic of China. After the Taiwan provincial authorities allowed Taiwanese compatriots to return to the mainland for family visits, the heirs of the pawnor, appellees Li Jinlian and Li Naping, promptly handled the relevant notarization procedures, entrusted a general agent ad litem, and filed a request with the people's court in 1989 to redeem the pawned house. Their claim complies with legal provisions and should be granted. Although travel between Taiwan and the Philippines was possible, the appellant did not provide evidence of any contact between the pawnor and the pawnee at the time of the expiration of the pawn period, or that the pawnor had the conditions to redeem the pawned house but failed to do so. The appellant, as one of the heirs of the pawnee Ke Boxing, manages the house in dispute, which does not violate the law, and has resided there for a long time; his participation in this lawsuit is appropriate. Therefore, the appellant's grounds of appeal are untenable. During the second instance trial, the appellees expressed willingness to increase the pawn consideration to RMB 6,000, which should be granted. Accordingly, on December 6, 1990, Xiamen Intermediate People's Court rendered judgment: Appellees Li Jinlian and Li Naping shall pay appellant Ke Jiesheng a pawn consideration of RMB 6,000; the original judgment permitting Li Jinlian and Li Naping to redeem the pawned house is affirmed.
